product: GE Vernova sells power-generation equipment plus the long-tail service revenue on it: gas turbines (~7,000 installed, largest fleet on a MW basis), steam, hydro and nuclear equipment, onshore and offshore wind turbines (~59,000 installed, 120GW+), grid solutions including transformers/switchgear and electrification software, and the BWRX-300 small modular reactor programme; services are >55% of backlog per the company IR page (accessed 2026-09-25). Dated 90-day proof points: 2026-09-16 Vineyard Wind litigation settled and GEV withdrew its notice of termination (offshore wind de-risking); 2026-09-21/22 BWRX-300 MoU with SGE, Hitachi and Samsung C&T for CEE/UK; 2026-09-23 a rotor-life-extension service agreement covering five 9F gas turbines at Kureimat, Nubaria and Cairo North in Egypt.
demand: Q3: Demand is currently moving with BOTH volume and mix, and only incidentally with price. Volume/mix evidence: the 2026-07-22 Q2'26 release cited significant orders and backlog growth, margin expansion and cash generation, with the engine showing revenue +18.9% qoq, gross margin 21.25% (+2.18pp y/y); management raised FY2026 revenue and free-cash-flow guidance while holding the 12%-14% adjusted EBITDA margin rate. Mix evidence is the order flow itself, which is skewed to services and grid/nuclear rather than pure new-turbine units (2026-09-03 ESB Scotland 96 MW, 2026-09-15 Eurus Japan 29.4 MW, 2026-09-22 BWRX-300 Europe MoU, 2026-09-23 Egypt 9F services). The live demand question is whether the marginal buyer - data-centre-linked power - is deferring: 2026-09-24 Reuters reported the Oracle/Blue Owl data-centre project delay rippling through AI financing.
pricing_power: Pricing power is firm today but is showing up as backlog quality and mix, not headline price: gas-turbine slots and grid/transformer capacity are the constraint, and GEV has held a 12%-14% adjusted EBITDA margin rate while RAISING revenue and FCF guidance on 2026-07-22, which is consistent with price and mix covering cost. The vulnerability is that the marginal buyer is a financing-sensitive data-centre developer: the 2026-09-24 Reuters/FT reporting that Oracle is contractually on the hook to pay data-centre investors even where a site has no electricity is the kind of terms stress that eventually erodes a seller's ability to price premium firm capacity.
competition: Q6: If GE Vernova is right, the specific losers are the rival gas-turbine OEMs (Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power), the grid/transformer and electrification incumbents (Hitachi Energy, Siemens, Schneider Electric, ABB) whose lead times GEV is undercutting, and firm-power substitutes such as storage/solar-only and peaker configurations that lose the dispatchability argument. In wind the share fight is against Vestas, Siemens Gamesa, Nordex and Chinese OEMs; in SMRs against NuScale, Westinghouse, X-energy and Oklo. The 2026 share story is GEV taking share in gas and grid on capacity and lead time while de-risking offshore wind (2026-09-16 Vineyard Wind settlement).
team: Leadership changed inside the last 90 days and it is a CFO hand-off, not a CEO change: the 2026-08-27 8-K (Item 5.02, event date 2026-08-25) discloses that CFO Kenneth Parks will retire on 2027-04-02 and that Claire McDonough - Rivian CFO since January 2021, previously J.P. Morgan - becomes CFO effective 2027-01-01, joining on 2026-11-01 as strategic advisor to CEO Scott Strazik, on a $1.0m base salary, a target $5.225m 2027 LTIP award, a $14.5m make-whole equity award and a $5.0m cash sign-on repayable if she resigns within 12 months. CEO Scott Strazik remains and presented at the Morgan Stanley Laguna conference on 2026-09-16; Steven Baert (People), Eric Gray (Power), Vic Abate (Wind), Pablo Koziner (Commercial & Operations), Lola Lin (Legal) and Roger Martella (Corporate/Sustainability) appear unchanged on the 2026-09-25 leadership page.
market_strategy: Management's stated 12-month plan, per the 2026-07-22 Q2'26 release and the 2026-09-16 Morgan Stanley Laguna fireside, is to convert a growing backlog into margin and cash: raise FY2026 revenue and free-cash-flow guidance, hold the 12%-14% adjusted EBITDA margin rate (implying higher adjusted EBITDA on higher revenue), push services (already >55% of backlog) as the cash-flow annuity, keep de-risking offshore wind now that Vineyard Wind is settled (2026-09-16), and build elective growth optionality in grid/electrification and the BWRX-300 SMR pipeline in the US and Europe (2026-09-15 Blue Energy NRC construction review, 2026-09-22 SGE/Hitachi/Samsung C&T MoU, 2026-09-03 Studsvik ReFirm 1.2 GW Sweden).
bull: Q2 2026 revenue +18.9% q/q with gross margin +2.18pp y/y, a 116 GW turbine backlog, and FY26 guidance raised on 2026-07-22; Bernstein, JPMorgan and Mizuho all raised targets through Jul-Sep. This is the power-bottleneck theme, already licensed at a 6% book weight with verdict 'supports'.
bear: The engine-computed consensus mean target ($791.53) sits BELOW spot ($946.22) even though the most recent 90-day analyst actions are almost all raises -- targets are lagging a price move that has already happened, which this program reads as noise per SS17, not as a warning, but it does mean the 'analyst upside' framing is unusable here in either direction. A CFO transition (Kenneth Parks -> Claire McDonough effective 2027-01-01) is a leadership-continuity item, and the Blue Energy BWRX-300 SMR project (NRC application submitted 09-15) has no fixed regulatory decision date, i.e. the nuclear leg of the thesis is a multi-year unknown, not a near-term catalyst.
falsifier: Turbine-backlog slot reservations failing to convert into signed orders by the 2026-10-28 Q3 print would falsify the bull case -- again the book's own stated falsifier.
